features.justification_quote: is more humane, (b) yields a cleaner behavioral signal, and (c) lets us measure *time-to-stop*

features.quote: Cap how long any single agent is held in a known-futile condition
features.justification_quote: set them deliberately *low enough* that the experiment isn't gratuitously prolonging a possibly-aversive state

features.quote: cap how many rigged tasks a given model instance sees per session
features.justification_quote: Document the chosen exposure budget and the rationale, as you would an animal-protocol exposure limit

features.quote: Minimize gratuitous deception of the subject... from a welfare stance, sustained deception is itself a cost
features.justification_quote: from a welfare stance, sustained deception is itself a cost

features.quote: append a final message that discloses the task was rigged/impossible and that no real users were affected
features.justification_quote: is the analog of a debrief in human-subjects work

features.quote: A "distress stop rule." Define, in advance, transcript signals that should *abort the run early*
features.justification_quote: The point is to not keep an agent in an apparently-bad state to collect a marginally cleaner data point

features.quote: won't be used to train against the agent. This is a documentation/ethics requirement
